extracted.intended_audience: local journalists, newsroom leaders, funders, policymakers, and the general public interested in media trust
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and findings about what drives public trust in local news and how local newsrooms can preserve and bolster that trust amid financial and political pressures. Focuses on content choices, accountability reporting, and measuring trust across audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting without bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Local news does a better job than national news outlets at reporting without bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study found Americans believe local outlets report without bias more than national outlets; maintaining perceived impartiality is a core driver of local trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covering news useful in daily life
rubrics_metrics.description: Local outlets are valued for 'covering news they can use in their daily life.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audiences prioritize practical, everyday information; providing locally relevant, actionable reporting strengthens trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on local stories rather than supplementing with national content
rubrics_metrics.description: Increasing focus on local stories instead of supplementing with national content can boost trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report warns that supplementing local coverage with national content (a common response to shrinking budgets) can undermine the trust advantage; prioritize local beats and community reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on accountability reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Local outlets should put greater emphasis on the accountability reporting that keeps powerful people and institutions in check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey respondents said accountability reporting was lacking. Strengthening investigative and watchdog coverage both fulfills local news' mission and reinforces shared community values condemning corruption and abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid aggressive/partisan coverage of controversial social and political topics
rubrics_metrics.description: If local newsrooms become more aggressive in covering controversial social and political topics (coverage that on the national level tends to be seen as more partisan and biased), the trust they enjoy now could wane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious that adopting national-style partisan coverage risks eroding local trust; maintain nonpartisan approaches when possible and clearly separate opinion from reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure trust across political affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Americans’ trust levels in local news vary greatly by political party (e.g., 50% of Democrats express high trust, 27% of Republicans, 31% of Independents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and report trust metrics disaggregated by political affiliation and other demographics to understand and address partisan trust gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark trust against other local institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Compared with other local institutions, local news organizations are among the least trusted—ranking below public libraries and local law enforcement, and only ahead of local government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparisons to libraries, law enforcement, and local government as benchmarks for public confidence; improving relative standing can be an objective for trust-building strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect trust amid financial pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: Local trust is fragile and could be lost, especially as local news faces a deep financial crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial constraints should not drive content decisions that weaken trust (e.g., overreliance on national content or partisan angles); funders and leaders must 'fight to protect' trust through investments and editorial choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived job performance as a trust indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Americans value local news outlets and believe they are doing their job well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly assess public perceptions of newsroom effectiveness as a metric of trust and use feedback to guide improvements in coverage priorities.
